About Event

NOTE : By registering for the Luma, you are submitting an application to participate. We will reach out on a rolling basis to let you know whether you've been accepted. There are a limited number of devices, we can support up to 200 participants .
This event is sponsored by Meta, Qualcomm, GitHub, Open Intelligence Foundation, and the PyTorch Foundation.
Join developers, researchers, and builders for the upcoming ExecuTorch Hackathon on October 17 -18 at Founder’s Inc., officially part of Open Source AI Week 2026 .
Hosted in collaboration with Qualcomm , Meta , GitHub , the PyTorch Foundation , and Open Intelligence Foundation , this hands-on event will challenge teams to build innovative AI experiences powered by ExecuTorch —an open-source framework for deploying and running PyTorch models efficiently on edge and on-device hardware.
Participants will work in teams of 3–5 people and select one of three tracks outlined below. Each team will receive a device from their selected track to use during the event. Builders will also get access to GitHub Copilot Pro+ to support their builds.
Compute Track
Build AI applications optimized for the Copilot+ PC powered by Snapdragon® X Elite processors, exploring the potential of powerful, efficient on-device AI computing.
Mobile + XR Track
Create AI-powered experiences for the Samsung Galaxy S25 Ultra powered by Snapdragon 8 Elite and Samsung Galaxy XR powered by Snapdragon® XR2+ Gen 2 processor, with a focus on mobile intelligence, immersive interaction, and multimodal applications.
IoT Track
Develop intelligent edge and embedded applications using the Arduino ® VENTUNO™ Q boards , combining on-device AI with real-time sensing, control, and connected experiences.
To participate, interested teams must select a track, form a team of 3–5, and submit a project proposal by October 4. Selected teams will be announced by October 7.
Prizes
The top team in each track will receive a prize package for every member of the team: Meta AI glasses and an Arduino® UNO™ Q. Build a standout project, demonstrate the potential of on-device AI, and take home hardware to continue exploring the edge.

GitHub will also award a one-year subscription to Copilot Pro to the winner.
Whether you are an experienced edge AI developer or eager to explore the future of open-source, on-device intelligence, the ExecuTorch Hackathon is an opportunity to collaborate, experiment, and build with the latest hardware and software across compute, mobile, XR, and IoT.
Questions? Join our Discord!
Ask questions about the event, connect with other participants, form a team, receive event announcements, and stay up to date throughout the hackathon.
👉 Join here: Join Discord Server
Bring your ideas. Build with ExecuTorch. Help shape the future of open-source, on device AI.

The Open Intelligence Foundation is a community-first nonprofit founded to protect, strengthen, and advance open-source AI, open models, and open science. Supported by a large community of volunteers and organizations, it takes a bottom-up approach to collaboration, working with academia and researchers to support research, development, and education in open-source AI. The foundation also leads Open Source AI Week , a community-run initiative celebrating open-source AI.

Founders, Inc. backs early-stage founders in emerging tech with first checks and 55,000 sq. ft. of lab space in San Francisco's Fort Mason. They run year-round programs to help ambitious builders to go from early stage to scalable companies.

About Event

🗓 Event Format
The Executable World is a one-day, in-person Full-Stack AI Hackathon, Demo Day, and Networking Mixer taking place on September 19, 2026 .
🚀 Prize Pool: $270,000 (Credit+Cash)
All official building, project submission, judging, demonstrations, awards, and networking will take place in person during the event.
The hackathon challenges, co-host and sponsor resources, judging criteria, and team-formation information will be released online one day before the event , giving participants time to understand the challenges, form teams, and prepare their development environments.

The event is co-hosted and supported by:
VeloDB

Each co-host and sponsor will contribute technology, technical resources, product guidance, workshops, mentors, judging support, or challenge opportunities for participating teams.

👉 [ Handbook ]

Review the hackathon tracks and challenge statements

Explore co-host and sponsor technologies

Access technical documentation and resources

Create participant profiles

Post or explore project ideas

Find potential teammates

Select a track

Define an initial product direction

Prepare their development environments

2–5 participants per team
Cross-functional teams combining engineering, product, design, AI infrastructure, and enterprise domain expertise are encouraged.

🔵 8:30–9:00 AM | Doors Open
The venue opens for organizers, co-hosts, sponsors, mentors, and early-arriving participants.
👥 9:00–10:00 AM | Participant Check-In & Final Team Formation
Participants check in, meet other builders, confirm their teams, review the challenges, and prepare their development environments.
Final team matching will be available for participants who arrive without a complete team.
🚀 10:00–10:10 AM | Opening Remarks
Welcome from the organizers and an introduction to The Executable World .
The opening will cover:
Hackathon tracks

Challenge statements

Judging criteria

Submission requirements

Event schedule

Co-host and sponsor resources

🧩 10:10–10:30 AM | Co-host & Sponsor Workshops
Technology leaders from Tencent EdgeOne and WorkBuddy will deliver short, practical sessions introducing their platforms, tools, APIs, technical resources, and suggested hackathon use cases.
Each company will have approximately 10–15 minutes to:
Introduce its technology

Present relevant APIs, platforms, or infrastructure

Explain available technical resources

Share example use cases

Help teams understand how its technology can be incorporated into a project

💻 10:30 AM–3:15 PM | In-Person Build Sprint
Teams design, build, test, and prepare working AI products across the hackathon tracks.
Support may include:
Co-host and sponsor technical assistance

Mentor office hours

Enterprise use-case feedback

Product and pitch guidance

Submission support

Demo preparation

Lunch and light refreshments will be available during the build sprint so teams can continue working.
✅ 3:15–3:30 PM | Final Submission
All teams submit their completed projects through the official hackathon platform.
Each submission may include:
Project name and description

Team information

Selected track

Product screenshots or demo video

Technology stack

Co-host or sponsor tools used

Repository or product link

Presentation materials

In-person and remote judges will review and score the submitted projects through the platform.
🎤 4:00–5:00 PM | Judges Panel — Building the Executable AI Stack
While judges review the submissions, technology leaders from ServiceNow and TikTok will discuss how different layers of the AI stack come together to create systems capable of executing real-world tasks.
Discussion topics may include:
Real-time data infrastructure for AI applications

Building and deploying production-ready AI agents

Visual memory and multimodal intelligence

Cloud infrastructure for scalable AI systems

Reliability, security, and observability

Moving AI products from prototype to production

What founders need to build defensible AI companies

How infrastructure companies can support the next generation of AI builders

The panel will be followed by a short audience Q&A.

Selected teams will present their products on the main stage.
The final demo format will be determined by the number of completed submissions.
If there are 10 or fewer teams , each team may receive approximately three minutes to demonstrate its project.
If there are more than 10 teams, judges will select a group of finalists to present on the main stage.
Winning teams may be announced one at a time, followed by a short product demonstration and award presentation from each selected team.
The program may include:

Overall hackathon awards

Builders, founders, enterprise leaders, co-hosts, sponsors, mentors, and investors connect around:
Product pilots

About Event

Build It. Test It. Prove It.
Smells like a hackathon. Runs like a pressure test, on you, not just your idea.
Proving Ground runs a three-day Sprint where judges push past the pitch. No script survives real questions about what you tried, what broke, and what you changed.
Past teams have gone on to raise from 500 Global and Blitzscaling Ventures, and been accepted into Berkeley SkyDeck and Confluent's accelerator, independently, without Proving Ground's involvement in those decisions.
What this is
A hackathon judges what you built by the end. We watch during the process and look past the end to what may come next.

The team is almost everything. How you make decisions under pressure, how you handle a setback, how you treat each other when something breaks. You'll document that as you go. What we ask you to show and how we question it are built around behavior, not performance.
How it works
Over three days, founders build under real constraint. No script, no rehearsed demo. Judges probe what you tried, what broke, and what you changed, and compare where you started to where you ended.
Two Tracks
Discovery Track. Pre-market, no active customer contact yet. For the startup curious, including enterprise folks seriously exploring a leap.
Pre-seed Track. In-market, already talking to customers. Ship something real, show what's changed, pressure-test your next move.
After the Sprint
Select teams get invited into the Street Test: 30 days back in the real world, no artificial deadline, no audience. This is where we see if momentum was real or borrowed from the room. It's the part a hackathon can't offer, because a hackathon ends when the weekend does.
